title: Plant a seedling: hold it upright in the hole with one hand while tipping the soil in with the other, then let it stand
instruction: Plant the seedling: take it out of its little cell, stand it upright in the middle of the planting hole and keep holding it while you tip the tray of soil into the hole around it, then let go so that it stands upright on its own.
context: Planting a seedling or a young tree is done the same way in every garden and nursery: one hand holds the plant upright in the middle of the hole while the other fills in the soil around it, and only once the soil is packed around the root ball can the plant be let go. A root ball set down in an empty hole on its own falls over, and soil poured in afterwards fixes it leaning. The same hold-it-upright-while-filling is used to set fence posts, plant stakes and parasol poles.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A fixed wooden potting bench 5 cm tall covers the table from 18 to 46 cm forward and from 14 cm right to 16 cm left of the centre line, with a square planting hole 10 x 10 cm and 4.8 cm deep in it, centred 34 cm forward and 3 cm left. A seedling (80 g) stands in a fixed black nursery cell (4.4 x 4.4 cm inside, 4.5 cm deep) on the bench 26 cm forward and 8 cm left: its root plug is 4 cm across and 4.5 cm tall with a round bottom (most of its weight), its stem is 0.8 cm square and reaches 15 cm, and three leaves 5 cm long cross at its top. Because the plug's bottom is round, the seedling falls over when it is not held or packed in. A blue tray (60 g; 8 cm wide, 10 cm deep, 2.5 cm walls, open at the front, with a 4 cm handle post just behind its back wall) lies on the bench on the near-right side of the hole, its open front reaching 1 cm over the hole's edge; in it are 45 soil clods (1.4 cm cubes, 3 g each) in two layers. The seedling, the tray and the clods are loose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler and a protractor; partial credit is the best reached during the run. 1.0: the seedling stands upright (within 10 degrees) in the hole, its plug in the middle (within 2 cm of the hole's centre) and down on the hole's floor (within 1.5 cm), standing on its own (both grippers 3.5 cm or more from it), with at least 32 of the 45 clods in the hole, the seedling still for 2 s. 0.5: the seedling upright in the middle of the hole with at least 32 clods in, but still held. 0.25: the seedling upright in the middle of the hole with at least 10 clods in. 0.0: anything else (a seedling left leaning, sitting on top of the soil or off centre scores 0).
reset_notes: Put the seedling back in its cell and the 45 clods back in the tray, the tray back at the hole's edge; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the soil is 45 rigid cubes; the seedling is one rigid body (a sphere and a cylinder for the root plug, a box stem, three box leaves) whose mass follows its shapes' volumes; the bench and the cell are fixed boxes; friction is set (seedling 0.8, tray 0.7, clods 0.3). Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
